chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Ja'far, from his father (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him) forbade taking out the weapons during the two Eids, except if there happens to be an enemy present.

key_terms.الْعِيدَيْنِ: The two Eids (Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on carrying weapons during Eid prayers in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq clarifies the etiquette of Eid prayers by prohibiting the display of weapons to maintain an atmosphere of peace and joy, unless a specific military threat necessitates readiness. This ruling underscores the distinction between ceremonial celebration and active combat, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on balancing spiritual tranquility with practical security during communal gatherings.
